data.body:
=== HEADLINE AC: THE INBOUND HALF IS NOW PROVEN. THE OUTBOUND HALF IS NOT. ===

GitHub Actions run 30660546548, job "jira DC harness smoke (real Jira Data Center, ephemeral)",
against main @ fde6baae7 (the first main containing the FIXED provenance oracle).

    [jira-live-canary] collected=17 executed=17 skipped=0
    1 failed, 16 passed in 13.55s

`executed=17 skipped=0` matters as much as the pass count: nothing silently skipped, so the canary
that exists to catch an all-skip green has nothing to hide. The single failure is
`test_the_documented_setup_refuses_to_read_the_pat_from_config` — the KNOWN, understood
[rebar:cd78-d877-3d25-4ec3] defect whose fix is in review as change 1127 and already holds
Verified +1. It is unrelated to the criterion below.

PROVEN — "an issue created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound pass":
`test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` PASSED. It creates an issue directly on
the DC harness through the real transport, runs a `bootstrap-strict` pass, and now asserts:
  * a local ticket exists whose id EQUALS `_jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key)` — exact match on the
    derived id, not a substring scan;
  * the BINDING STORE maps that local id to the DC key — i.e. the local ticket genuinely corresponds
    to THAT issue, which is what the criterion is actually about;
  * `creation_channel == "jira"` — the shared family channel, with the deployment distinguished by
    `RemoteRef.instance` rather than a second channel.

WHY THIS IS THE FIRST REAL EVIDENCE, AND WHY EARLIER SIGNALS WERE NOT. Three defects masked this in
sequence, each hiding the next:
  1. the run reported `scanned=0` and "converged" — it converged because the store was EMPTY, so
     "converged" and "works" were indistinguishable;
  2. the PAT-cap bug [rebar:f391-806b-938f-45d8] killed the suite at SETUP, so the test never ran;
  3. the oracle itself could not pass [rebar:23ed-de0a-765b-49aa] — it grepped the RAW Jira key
     (`RBJ...-1`) against a payload whose id is lowercased (`jira-rbj...-1`) and which carries no raw
     key at all, so a correctly-created ticket produced a RED and a broken one would have too.
Only with all three fixed does this test's verdict carry information. That is why its previous red was
NOT evidence of breakage, and why this green IS evidence of function.

NOT PROVEN — "a local edit appears on the DC issue after an outbound pass". I checked rather than
assumed: `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py` contains exactly three live tests
(no-unhandled-exception, repeated-pass-writes-nothing, and the provenance test above). NONE mutates a
local ticket and asserts the change surfaces on the DC issue. So the outbound half of the epic's
headline AC remains unproven, and [rebar:5200-e04e-246e-4aae] (J11) is exactly the story that must
supply it. The epic must NOT be closed on this run alone.

What IS additionally established by this run: a full writing `bootstrap-strict` pass against a real DC
instance raises no unhandled exception, and an immediately repeated pass writes nothing (idempotence)
— both covering criteria for [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36].
